# Quantum Mixing Depth

This repository studies the minimum depth needed to mix an entire unknown quantum
register under deterministic unitary gate layers followed by fixed local
depolarization. Every input qubit and every retained output is part of the task;
the half-diamond error includes arbitrary input-reference entanglement.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: question, optimal-depth table, scientific and learning routes,
  reproduction, scope, purpose and contact.
- science/model.md: authoritative model and quantifiers; Theorem G for regular
  lattices, Theorem A for unrestricted pairs, Proposition P for passive noise.
- science/channel_distance.md: exact noisy-Clifford Pauli reduction, Pauli-channel
  diamond distance, Fourier chi-square normalization, and block tensorization.
- science/causal_bound.md: arbitrary-unitary inverse-observable converse; physical
  joint POVMs on disjoint full syntactic cones; finite architecture bounds.
- science/geometric_construction.md: elementary line branch-weight existence,
  inherited nearest-neighbor compiler, recursive coordinate sequence, rectangular
  checkpoint lemma, finite error bounds, and tiling without added qubits.
- science/unrestricted_connectivity.md: exact imported Pauli-spreading theorem,
  low-weight union bound, no-auxiliary complete-mixing conversion and block sizes.
- science/passive.md: exact binomial expression for the passive diamond error,
  finite upper/lower bounds and leading logarithmic depth.
- science/finite_examples.md: finite circuits, checkpoint weights, direct channel
  calculations and the relation of those checks to the general proofs.
- science/interpretation.md: spacetime exposure to noise, global versus local
  relaxation, resource accounting, physical interpretation and limits.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: inherited mechanisms, precise primary dependencies,
  and distinctions from error mitigation, sampling, and dissipative reachability.
- references/references.bib: bibliographic metadata and source versions.
- learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md: the selected Watrous (2018) educational anchor,
  verified section pointers, notation and normalization translations, and the
  steps connecting textbook foundations to the project's proofs.
- learning/MILESTONES.md: exactly M01 through M30, ordered through background /
  preliminaries and narrative / innovation; understanding targets, dependencies,
  conceptual connections and source pointers for the complete scientific story.
- verification/README.md: reproducibility commands, coverage and limitations.
- verification/run_all.py: deterministic finite verification runner.

Reader routes:
- Story: model, passive benchmark, interpretation, then the two matching proofs.
- Study: Watrous bridge, the milestone map, and the linked canonical science;
  use finite examples to connect the abstract objects with concrete circuits.
- Geometric theorem: model, channel distance, causal bound, geometric construction.
- Unrestricted theorem: model, causal bound, channel distance, unrestricted
  connectivity, and the stated primary spreading theorem.
- Reproduction: verification README, runner and expected outputs; keep finite
  observations separate from universal proof.
- Attribution: related work before making a novelty claim.

Preserve these distinctions:
- Noise retention eta lies strictly between zero and one and is fixed with size.
- Every charged layer includes noise on all sites, including idle sites.
- The circuit is fixed independently of the unknown input.
- No auxiliary qubits, resets, measurements, discarded outputs or runtime random
  controls are supplied to the upper constructions.
- The maximally mixed replacer is the target; pure-state cooling is a different task.
- Complete-channel error is stronger than uniform outcomes in one basis or decay
  of local observables.
- The geometric upper concerns regular filled boxes; the lower is broader.
- Dimension and target global error are fixed in the asymptotic laws.
- The inverse final Clifford is analytical only and is never executed.
- The inverse-noise maps in the lower bound are not physical operations; the
  resulting bounded witness POVMs are physical.
- Clifford compilation and the all-to-all spreading theorem are imported.
- Scrambling-enhanced noisy mixing is established prior work.
- The all-to-all source is a versioned 2026 preprint; the geometric proof uses
  established linear-neighbor Clifford synthesis.
- Do not infer continuous driven-Hamiltonian wall-time optimality, optimized
  constants, practical device advantage, or quantum-over-classical advantage.
- Verification results support finite identities, not external peer review.
- Watrous (2018) is the single educational anchor. The bridge distinguishes its
  foundations from locally supplied derivations and imported research theorems.
